goal: Let the user open text that is cut short to read it whole
how: .text-clamp-2 or -3 cuts the block after two or three lines, and a button with data-clamp-toggle and aria-controls opens it in full and closes it again; both labels are the app's. Where the text fits, the button is not shown.
avoid: Cutting text the reader needs with .text-truncate and no way to read the rest.

goal: Let the user scroll a long or wide block without scrolling the page
how: .sedna-scroll caps a block's height, --sm, --md, --lg or --scroll-max, and .sedna-scroll-x lets a wide table scroll sideways inside the page; both fade the cut edge. Give the scroller tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label.
avoid: A scroller with no tab stop and no name, which a keyboard reader cannot scroll and a screen reader cannot describe.

goal: Let the user print a page without the app's own chrome
how: The frame drops itself from paper already; .sedna-no-print keeps the app's own controls off it, and .sedna-print-only adds what only the sheet needs, such as a reference number or a signature line.
avoid: Writing a print stylesheet that hides library classes, which breaks on the next release.

goal: Let the user reach a bar of the app's own on a phone with a notch or a home indicator
how: With viewport-fit=cover on the host page, .sedna-safe-bottom, -top and -inline pad the element carrying the background by the strip the device has taken, and by nothing where there is none.
avoid: Putting the class on a wrapper, whose padding leaves a transparent band where the device's strip is.
